title: AI Guard with the LiteLLM proxy: LiteLLM's native zscaler_ai_guard guardrail as the README describes it, and the SDK-based callback example

prose.text: The LiteLLM folder offers two routes: a guardrail that ships inside LiteLLM itself, whose code is not in this repository, and an example callback built on the Zscaler Python SDK. {{native}} {{native-endpoint}} Whether execute-policy works without a policy ID is open in [[ai-security.ai-guard.runtime-api:execute-without-policy-id]].

prose.label: The SDK callback.
prose.text: {{callback-hooks}} {{callback-skips}} {{callback-verdict}} What LiteLLM does with the callback's exceptions, and whether the hooks run for streamed responses, is open {{gap:hook-behavior}}.

prose.label: SDK version.
prose.text: {{sdk-unpinned}} The SDK release that fixed detection authentication is in [[ai-security.ai-guard.runtime-api:sdk-bearer]].

checks.do: For the native guardrail, whether a policy_id is configured; its default endpoint is execute-policy.

native.statement: The README describes LiteLLM's built-in `zscaler_ai_guard` guardrail, configured in config.yaml with `mode` `during_call` for input and `post_call` for output, an API key, an optional base URL and policy ID, per-request overrides through `metadata.zguard_policy_id`, per-team and per-key policies, and forwarding of user information.

quotes: The native plugin uses `guardrail: zscaler_ai_guard` directly in your `config.yaml` and supports `during_call` (input) and `post_call` (output) modes, per-request/team/key policy overrides, and user info forwarding.

api_key: os.environ/ZSCALER_AI_GUARD_API_KEY
      api_base: os.environ/ZSCALER_AI_GUARD_URL        # Optional, defaults to us1
      policy_id: os.environ/ZSCALER_AI_GUARD_POLICY_ID  # Optional

native-endpoint.statement: The example native configuration notes that `api_base` defaults to `https://api.us1.zseclipse.net/v1/detection/execute-policy` and marks `policy_id` optional, and the README's comparison lists the native plugin's policy selection as an explicit policy ID.

callback-hooks.statement: The example callback is a LiteLLM CustomLogger: `async_pre_call_hook` scans the last user message (text parts joined) with direction IN, and `async_post_call_success_hook` scans the first choice that has message content with direction OUT, each through the SDK's `LegacyZGuardClientHelper` `resolve_and_execute_policy` with a fresh uuid4 transaction ID, run in a worker thread.

async def async_post_call_success_hook(self, data, user_api_key_dict, response):
"""Extract the last user message from the request."""

callback-skips.statement: When the request has no user content, or the response has no choice with message content (for example a tool-call-only reply), the callback returns without scanning.

callback-verdict.statement: The callback raises an HTTP 403 `HTTPException` unless the action is ALLOW or DETECT, so a missing action blocks; an SDK error is logged and raised as a plain Exception carrying the error text.

quotes: return str(action or "").upper() not in self.ALLOWED_ACTIONS

sdk-unpinned.statement: The callback's Dockerfile extends the LiteLLM `main-stable` image and installs `zscaler-sdk-python` with no version constraint; the key and cloud come from `AIGUARD_API_KEY` and `AIGUARD_CLOUD` (default us1).

quotes: AIGUARD_API_KEY   - Zscaler AI Guard API key

hook-behavior.title: How LiteLLM handles the callback's exceptions and streamed responses
hook-behavior.detail: The callback raises HTTPException(403) on a block and a plain Exception when the SDK reports an error, and scans responses only in async_post_call_success_hook. What LiteLLM returns to the client for the plain Exception (an error, so fail closed, or a logged pass) and whether that hook runs for streamed responses depends on LiteLLM, whose source is not registered.
